title: AI agent observability for TypeScript — Balsats
description: AI agent observability for TypeScript: spans for runs, model steps, tool calls and memory — exported to your collector over OTLP.
h1: AI agent observability — see what actually ran, in the stack you already use.

sections.heading: Spans for the things that actually ran
sections.body: Every agent run, model step, tool call, workflow run and step, and memory recall or save opens a span. The span model is Balsats's own minimal one — the framework doesn't require an OpenTelemetry SDK in order to trace.

sections.heading: A tracer you hand down once
sections.body: Assemble a tracer at the composition root and every agent built through the app traces with no per-agent wiring. A standalone agent with no tracer stays fully first-class: zero overhead, no span objects.

sections.heading: Export to where your telemetry already lives
sections.body: Console and memory exporters are built in; @balsats/otlp maps Balsats spans to GenAI semantic conventions and exports them to any OTLP-compatible collector. A resumed run opens a new span in the same trace, so one human interaction stays one story.

faq.question: What gets traced in a Balsats run?
faq.answer: Agent runs, model steps, tool calls, workflow runs and steps, and memory recalls and saves each open a span, with parent-child structure that keeps a run readable.

faq.question: Can I send traces to my existing OpenTelemetry backend?
faq.answer: Yes — @balsats/otlp exports Balsats spans with GenAI semantic conventions to any OTLP-compatible collector.

faq.question: Where do traces go if I don't configure anything?
faq.answer: Balsats ships console and memory exporters, so spans can be watched during development without running a collector; nothing is exported unless you assemble a tracer with an exporter.

faq.question: Does tracing cost anything when I don't want it?
faq.answer: No: a standalone new Agent() with no tracer opens no span objects, so an untraced run stays as small as it looks.

faq.question: Does Balsats ship a dashboard or a hosted observability service?
faq.answer: No. Balsats produces spans and exports them to the stack you operate; there is no Balsats-side service in the loop.
